extracted.intended_audience: heads of executive departments and agencies, senior federal officials, and tribal governments/representatives
extracted.subtask_short: White House Council on Native American Affairs
extracted.subtask_description: An Executive Order establishing an interagency White House Council to coordinate Federal policy and engagement with federally recognized tribes, defining its policy goals, membership, functions, meeting rules, funding support, and legal/implementation limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of government-to-government relationship and tribal sovereignty
rubrics_metrics.description: The United States recognizes a government-to-government relationship, as well as a unique legal and political relationship, with federally recognized tribes. Honoring these relationships and respecting the sovereignty of tribal nations is critical to advancing tribal self-determination and prosperity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This relationship is set forth in the Constitution, treaties, statutes, Executive Orders, administrative rules and regulations, and judicial decisions. The text emphasizes restoring and healing relations, and that tribal self-determination is necessary for successful and prospering communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: National policy to ensure coordinated, effective engagement and trust responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a national policy to ensure that the Federal Government engages in a true and lasting government-to-government relationship with federally recognized tribes in a more coordinated and effective manner, including by better carrying out its trust responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy is stated as a means of promoting and sustaining prosperous and resilient tribal communities; greater engagement and meaningful consultation with tribes is paramount when developing policies affecting tribal nations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy goal: promote sustainable economic development
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) promoting sustainable economic development, particularly energy, transportation, housing, other infrastructure, entrepreneurial, and workforce development to drive future economic growth and security;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a primary means to promote and sustain prosperous and resilient tribal communities; emphasis on multiple sectors (energy, transportation, housing, infrastructure, entrepreneurship, workforce).

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy goal: support greater access to and control over nutrition and healthcare
rubrics_metrics.description: (b) supporting greater access to, and control over, nutrition and healthcare, including special efforts to confront historic health disparities and chronic diseases;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on access and tribal control, and on addressing historic health disparities and chronic diseases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy goal: improve tribal justice systems and protect communities
rubrics_metrics.description: (c) supporting efforts to improve the effectiveness and efficiency of tribal justice systems and protect tribal communities;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes strengthening tribal justice capacity as part of improving quality of life and community protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy goal: expand and improve lifelong educational opportunities with tribal control
rubrics_metrics.description: (d) expanding and improving lifelong educational opportunities for American Indians and Alaska Natives, while respecting demands for greater tribal control over tribal education, consistent with Executive Order 13592;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically references respect for tribal control over education and connection to prior Executive Order 13592 concerning education and tribal colleges/universities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy goal: protect tribal lands, environments, resources, and cultures
rubrics_metrics.description: (e) protecting tribal lands, environments, and natural resources, and promoting respect for tribal cultures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protecting lands, environments and natural resources is expressed alongside promoting cultural respect as essential policy goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of the Council
rubrics_metrics.description: There is established the White House Council on Native American Affairs (Council). The Council shall improve coordination of Federal programs and the use of resources available to tribal communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Council is the designated vehicle to improve interagency coordination and resource use for tribal communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership composition and Chair
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of the Interior shall serve as the Chair of the Council, which shall also include the heads of a specified list of executive departments, agencies, and offices (State; Treasury; Defense; Justice; Agriculture; Commerce; Labor; HHS; HUD; Transportation; Energy; Education; VA; DHS; SSA; OPM; USTR; OMB; EPA; SBA; CEA; ONDCP; Domestic Policy Council; National Economic Council; OSTP; CEQ; White House Office of Public Engagement and Intergovernmental Affairs; Advisory Council on Historic Preservation; Denali Commission; White House Office of Cabinet Affairs; and such other entities as the Chair may designate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership is explicitly enumerated and allows the Chair to designate additional departments/agencies/offices as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation by members
rubrics_metrics.description: A member of the Council may designate a senior-level official, who is a full-time officer or employee of the Federal Government, to perform his or her functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits delegation to senior-level full-time federal officers or employees to carry out Council functions on behalf of members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of the Interior funding and administrative support
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of the Interior shall provide funding and administrative support for the Council to the extent permitted by law and within existing appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support is subject to applicable law and existing appropriations; not an open-ended funding mandate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy development coordination through Domestic Policy Council
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council shall coordinate its policy development through the Domestic Policy Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the Domestic Policy Council as the channel for coordinating policy development across agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outreach coordination through White House Office of Public Engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council shall coordinate its outreach to federally recognized tribes through the White House Office of Public Engagement and Intergovernmental Affairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designates the Office of Public Engagement as the responsible office for tribal outreach coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting frequency and invitation authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council shall meet three times a year, with any additional meetings convened as deemed necessary by the Chair. The Chair may invite other interested agencies and offices to attend meetings as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets a minimum regular meeting cadence (three times annually) and gives the Chair discretion to convene additional meetings and invite other participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: develop policy recommendations to support tribal self-governance and quality of life
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council shall work across executive departments, agencies, and offices to coordinate development of policy recommendations to support tribal self-governance and improve the quality of life for Native Americans, and shall coordinate the United States Government's engagement with tribal governments and their communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames the Council's core mission as interagency coordination to produce policy recommendations and coordinate government engagement with tribes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function: recommend policy priorities to the President
rubrics_metrics.description: (Sec. 4(a)) The Council shall make recommendations to the President, through the Director of the Domestic Policy Council, concerning policy priorities, including improving the effectiveness of Federal investments in Native American communities to increase impact and create greater opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations flow to the President via the Domestic Policy Council and emphasize improving Federal investment effectiveness and opportunity creation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function: coordinate Federal engagement with tribal stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: (Sec. 4(b)) The Council shall coordinate, through the Director of the Office of Public Engagement and Intergovernmental Affairs, Federal engagement with tribal governments and Native American stakeholders, including tribal consortia, small businesses, education and training institutions (including tribal colleges and universities), health-care providers, trade associations, research and grant institutions, law enforcement, State and local governments, and community and non-profit organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies a broad set of stakeholders and delegates coordination to the Office of Public Engagement via its Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function: coordinate process to honor tribal consultation commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: (Sec. 4(c)) The Council shall coordinate a more effective and efficient process for executive departments, agencies, and offices to honor the United States commitment to tribal consultation as set forth in Executive Order 13175 (Consultation and Coordination With Indian Tribal Governments) and the November 5, 2009 memorandum (Tribal Consultation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates coordination to improve procedures for honoring established tribal consultation commitments, referencing existing Executive Order and memorandum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function: assist in organizing White House Tribal Nations Conference
rubrics_metrics.description: (Sec. 4(d)) The Council shall assist the White House Office of Public Engagement and Intergovernmental Affairs in organizing the White House Tribal Nations Conference each year by bringing together leaders invited from all federally recognized Indian tribes and senior officials from the Federal Government for direct government-to-government discussion of policy priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies an annual conference role, facilitating direct government-to-government dialogue between tribal leaders and senior federal officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: General duty: agencies to assist and provide information
rubrics_metrics.description: (Sec. 5(a)) The heads of executive departments, agencies, and offices shall assist and provide information to the Council, consistent with applicable law, as may be necessary to carry out the functions of the Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires cooperation from agency heads subject to applicable law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-impairment of statutory authorities and OMB functions
rubrics_metrics.description: (Sec. 5(b)) Nothing in this order shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect: (i) the authority granted by law to an executive department, agency, or the head thereof; or (ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms that the Order does not alter statutory authorities or OMB's established functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation constraints: applicable law and appropriations
rubrics_metrics.description: (Sec. 5(c)) This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation is conditioned on compliance with law and available funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: federally recognized tribe
rubrics_metrics.description: (Sec. 5(d)) For purposes of this order, 'federally recognized tribe' means an Indian or Alaska Native tribe, band, nation, pueblo, village, or community that the Secretary of the Interior acknowledges to exist as an Indian tribe pursuant to the Federally Recognized Indian Tribe List Act of 1994, 25 U.S.C. 479a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the statutory reference and scope for what counts as a federally recognized tribe for Council purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: American Indian and Alaska Native
rubrics_metrics.description: (Sec. 5(e)) For purposes of this order, 'American Indian and Alaska Native' means a member of an Indian tribe, as membership is defined by the tribe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaves membership definition to each tribe's own rules; clarifies terminology used in the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: No enforceable private right created
rubrics_metrics.description: (Sec. 5(f)) This order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, its officers, employees, or agents, or any other person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States that the Order does not create enforceable legal rights or remedies.
